record.original_question:
Let A ∈ GL_n(R) and let Γ ⊂ R^n be a full rank lattice. A measurable set W ⊂ R^n is an (A,Γ)-wavelet set if {W+γ}_{γ∈Γ} partitions R^n modulo null sets and {A^j W}_{j∈Z} partitions R^n modulo null sets.

Characterize pairs (A,Γ) for which an (A,Γ)-wavelet set exists.

evidence.quote:
Problem 3.2. Characterize pairs of dilations A ∈ GLn (R) and lattices Γ ⊂ Rn for which
wavelet set exists.

Definition 3.2. Let (A, Γ) be a dilation-lattice pair. We say that W ⊂ Rn is an (A, Γ)-
wavelet set if
   (t) {W + γ}k∈Γ is a partition of Rn modulo null sets, and
   (d) {Aj W }j∈Z is a partition of Rn modulo null sets.

artifact.status_search_result: Existence is fully established for expansive dilations A (wavelet sets exist for every lattice Γ), and for general invertible A it is known that an (A,Γ)-wavelet set exists for a generic choice of lattice Γ; non-expansive cases are linked to a lattice counting estimate (Bownik–Lemvig and Speegle et al.). However, a complete characterization of all pairs (A,Γ) admitting a wavelet set is not known and is listed as an open problem in surveys on wavelet theory.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems in Wavelet Theory (Bownik)
status_evidence.snippet: Problem: Characterize pairs of dilations A and lattices Γ for which a wavelet set exists.
status_evidence.claim: Listed as an open problem in a survey of wavelet theory.

status_evidence.title: Wavelets for Non-expanding Dilations and the Lattice Counting Estimate
status_evidence.snippet: MSF wavelets exist for all invertible dilations A and a generic choice of lattice Γ; exceptional pairs form a thin set.
status_evidence.claim: Partial existence results: generic lattices admit wavelet sets; non-expansive cases tied to lattice counting estimate.
